step_rules.tools_not_allowed: the tools array is absent or empty
step_rules.content_not_allowed: every content part is exactly {type: 'text', text: string of at most 16000 chars}
step_rules.prompt_too_large: the sum of all content characters is at most 24000
step_rules.schema_invalid: also: the last message has role user
step_rules.turn_header_invalid: see turn_header.rules (system role, no later system message, header line, non-empty persona)

prompt_flattening.system: messages[0].content with the first line (the turn header) removed
prompt_flattening.prompt: for each message after the first: '### ' + role + LF + content + LF + LF
prompt_flattening.text_parts: a content array is its text parts joined with LF

brain.chat.finish_reason_rule: A completed answer always ends with finish_reason 'stop', with usage on that chunk. 'length' is never sent. This deviates from OpenAI on purpose: nanobot treats 'length' as 'continue' and calls again on a prompt it wrote. A token-capped answer stays visible in the model-call record (tokens_out equals max_tokens).
brain.chat.budget_rule: A turn is counted when the call is let into inference: after the inference slot is acquired, the cap is re-checked and the turn counted in one atomic step (refusal budget_exhausted, recorded as a model_call). Lab mode is re-checked at the same point. A call refused because the model is busy costs nothing.

turn_header.encoding: prefix + one-line JSON, then LF, then the persona (the system prompt)

response_schema_rules.serialization: JSON, separators , and :, UTF-8, no ASCII escaping

rules: No message after index 0 has role 'system'.
The text of messages[0] is its content string, or its text parts joined by LF. Its first line, up to the first LF, is the prefix followed by one-line JSON valid against 'schema'.
What follows that LF is not empty after stripping whitespace.

tools_not_allowed.message: Tools are not allowed on this edge.

brain_not_local.message: The lab's fast brain is not a local model.

brain_unavailable.message: The lab's fast brain is not available.

structured_output_unsupported.message: The lab's brain cannot do structured output.

stream_errors.brain_failed: The brain stopped before it finished.

errors.retry_note: nanobot retries on 408/409/429/5xx and on error text containing a transient marker (nanobot/providers/base.py _TRANSIENT_ERROR_MARKERS); an explicit X-Should-Retry: false is honoured first (LLMProvider.is_transient_response), so every error carries it, which also covers the hex digest in error.lab_contract_sha256 that can contain digit runs such as 500.

edge_events.note: Written by the edge itself; Buddy cannot send them (not in the trace.record event enum).

placeholders.$CONTRACT_SHA256: sha256 (hex) of the contract file bytes
placeholders.$NOW: current UTC time, RFC 3339, second resolution, suffix Z
placeholders.$NOW+<n>s / $NOW-<n>s: the same, n seconds later / earlier

setup_keys.brain: 'local' (default: ollama_native, loopback, llama-ai-eng, structured output, Built with Llama) | 'cloud' | 'none' | 'non_ollama' | 'no_structured_output'
setup_keys.calls_last_minute: admitted brain.chat calls by the same pseudonym in the last 60 s; default 0
setup_keys.brain_tokens: 'few' (default: the fake brain reports 12 completion tokens) | 'max' (it reports exactly max_tokens)

case_notes: A case runs against a fresh world built from 'setup'; 'followups' run in order against the same world.
'body_subset' means every key and value listed must equal the response body at that path; other keys are ignored.
Every response with status >= 400 must also carry errors.response_headers; the runners check it for all cases.
'edge_only' holds checks only ARAIL's real routes can make (trace ring, ledger rows); Buddy's FakeHost ignores it.
'$NOW' is read once per case and reused by every request in it, so a replayed request is byte-identical.
In 'body_subset', a list is matched element by element from index 0 for as many elements as the expectation lists.
'stream' checks the SSE response: media_type, the assembled delta content, the final finish_reason, a usage chunk, and the closing data: [DONE].
'brain_received' checks what the fake brain was called with: system, prompt, max_tokens, response_schema (only the keys listed).
